core.title: The URN layer segment must be one of the layer roles
core.given: A file declares the stack's component URN; the URN's layer segment is what the boundary and dependency-flow rules read to judge whether a dependency is legal.
core.when: You write or change the URN, or the layer-vocabulary check reports its layer as invalid.
core.then: Set the layer segment to exactly one of the layer roles — domain, application, integration, presentation, composition root — using the stack-local names the profile declares.
avoid: Inventing a new layer: the vocabulary is fixed by the core convention set, not by a stack realization; adding a layer is a core change.
unless: The URN is not of the component-URN shape the profile declares; it is skipped.
core.why: Layering rules read the layer segment to decide whether a dependency is legal. A layer outside the vocabulary is not just mislabelled: no layering rule can reach the file, so it becomes a hole that lets any dependency pass unchallenged.
evidence: The stack's layer-vocabulary check reports no finding for this obligation.
verification: Check the layer segment of each in-scope URN against the closed layer vocabulary: the five layer roles (domain, application, integration, presentation, composition root) under their stack-local names from the profile.
Skip URNs that do not match the component-URN shape the profile declares.
The vocabulary is owned by the core convention set, not by a stack realization; the check rejects realization-local additions to it.
Severity 3; disposition strict — the check fails on every finding, with no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

values: file that carries the stack's component URN
finding emitted by the layer-vocabulary check when the layer segment is outside the vocabulary

fires: A declared component URN has its layer segment set to a value outside the closed layer vocabulary (domain, application, integration, presentation, composition root).
The coder writes or edits a component URN.
doesNotFire: URNs that do not match the declared component-URN shape (skipped).
Repositories on other stacks: each stack realization of this obligation covers its own scope.

profileRequirements.meaning: The closed layer vocabulary the layer segment must come from, with each layer role's stack-local name (e.g. the composition root's local name).
The shape of the URN a source file declares, including which segment carries the layer, so the check knows which URNs are in scope and where the layer sits.
profileRequirements.bunValue: six-segment URN; segment 5 is the layer segment

profileRequirements.meaning: How a file is assigned its layer role (via the URN's layer segment) and that a file with no such URN is out of scope, not a violation.
profileRequirements.bunValue: the file's layer is segment 5 of its six-segment URN; files with no six-segment URN are skipped (out of scope)

bunOnly.text: file inspected by bun_green_traceability_detector that carries a six-segment URN
bunOnly.reason: The detector id is a realization detail and which observer inspects files is a realization concern; the concrete six-segment shape is profile data (urn.component), so only the detector reference and the segment-count detail are Bun-specific.

Finding ids of this rule are realization details: GREEN-URN-006 is the shared core alias carried by other stacks' realizations and BUN-GREEN-URN-LAYER-001 is Bun-only; the core describes the finding generically.

bunOnly.text: bun_green_traceability_detector reports no GREEN-URN-006 / BUN-GREEN-URN-LAYER-001 finding.
bunOnly.reason: Detector and finding ids are realization details; the core evidence is the generic 'the layer-vocabulary check reports no finding'.

neutralityNotes: The 'six-segment / segment 5' mechanics have no core wording: the core speaks of 'the layer segment' and the shape and position come from the profile (urn.component, roles.assignment), so instantiating with the Bun profile reproduces the exact Bun obligation. GREEN-URN-006 is a shared cross-realization alias, but as a finding id of this rule it is kept in bunOnly per the notProfileKeys rule; the core's verification names the check generically. The strict-disposition elaboration ('fails on every finding; no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline') is the shared disposition policy recorded in core:verification. Bun's local layer name 'assembly' appears only as the profile value for the composition-root layer role.
